bug_semantics: When queryDepth was configured, Mercurius enforced it on HTTP GraphQL operations but the separately parsed GraphQL subscription path accepted WebSocket start messages and called subscribe() without invoking queryDepth. A remote client could therefore submit arbitrarily deep recursive subscription selections and trigger disproportionate resolver work on every event, bypassing the configured denial-of-service guard.
flaw_origin: PR #78 introduced WebSocket subscriptions after queryDepth already existed. Decomposing its squash commit 8a2f9a59cab4475372e66394e1594be9c561c267 shows that the first member, aa4bc978e8d16a2e92dd9a4adfd830d7a328f587, created subscription.js with parse(query) followed directly by subscribe() and no queryDepth call. Its parent 6414c10e3cc98cd1fd1f46a457b2b719074c48af already enforced queryDepth in index.js for HTTP and had no WebSocket subscription implementation, so aa4bc978e8d16a2e92dd9a4adfd830d7a328f587 is the atomic BIC.
ai_marker: absent: atomic BIC aa4bc978e8d16a2e92dd9a4adfd830d7a328f587 has author and committer Peter Balazs <frikille@gmail.com>, message 'Initial commit for subscription support', and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, or other AI trailer in the commit object.
evidence: Live GitHub advisory GHSA-m4h2-mjfm-mp55 and the CVE.org CVE-2026-30241 record both describe WebSocket subscription queryDepth bypass, mark versions < 16.8.0 affected, and identify 16.8.0 as patched; CVE.org state is PUBLISHED and the GHSA withdrawn_at is null.

Local full-history clone is non-shallow. git grep 6414c10e3cc98cd1fd1f46a457b2b719074c48af shows index.js already loading queryDepth and checking document.definitions, while git ls-tree confirms that parent has no subscription.js or subscription-connection.js WebSocket path.

GitHub's PR #78 API reports base 6414c10e3cc98cd1fd1f46a457b2b719074c48af, 36 members, head f5e334bb1ac25ae29387eb57948c23677877a45a, and squash 8a2f9a59cab4475372e66394e1594be9c561c267; the head and squash trees are identical at 697b9e791c7146114aeebaed64c008cc55f2c090.

GitHub commit API for first PR member aa4bc978e8d16a2e92dd9a4adfd830d7a328f587 shows parent 6414c10e3cc98cd1fd1f46a457b2b719074c48af and a newly added subscription.js that parses the WebSocket payload then calls subscribe() without queryDepth; this is the smallest member that writes the vulnerable path.

The aa4bc978e8d16a2e92dd9a4adfd830d7a328f587 commit object names Peter Balazs as both author and committer, contains only the message 'Initial commit for subscription support', and has no AI attribution marker.
The equivalent squash 8a2f9a59cab4475372e66394e1594be9c561c267 is not in v1.5.0 and is in v2.0.0, establishing the first vulnerable release boundary for the newly introduced subscription feature.

git show 5b56f60f4b0d60780b0ff499a479bd830bdd6986 and its parent proves the direct fix: it passes queryDepthLimit through index.js, lib/routes.js, and lib/subscription.js, then calls queryDepth(document.definitions, this.queryDepthLimit) in lib/subscription-connection.js before execution; that guard is absent in parent 249809aed8c6bcb98c1d53404c6896b32e1f29e1.
git merge-base --is-ancestor shows fix 5b56f60f4b0d60780b0ff499a479bd830bdd6986 is absent from v16.7.0 and present in v16.8.0, matching the advisory's patched boundary.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and its lifecycle closes. HTTP queryDepth enforcement predates subscriptions. The decomposed PR #78 first member aa4bc978e8d16a2e92dd9a4adfd830d7a328f587 created the separate WebSocket parse-and-subscribe path without carrying over the existing depth validation; the immediate parent has the HTTP guard but no such path. The 36-member PR head is tree-identical to the mainline squash, and the squash enters v2.0.0. Commit 5b56f60f4b0d60780b0ff499a479bd830bdd6986 directly adds the missing option plumbing and pre-execution depth check, landing in v16.8.0 after v16.7.0. The atomic BIC commit object has only human author/committer metadata and no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
